verdict.line: You lose if he lands Footwork (E) shields and Path Maker (W) stuns in point-blank trades before level 6; you win if you poke from outside 525 range and let Muramana-charged Shock Blasts whittle him down after level 11.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's Footwork (E) shield-dash and Path Maker (W) stun/knockback let him force short, point-blank trades that beat Jayce's melee Hammer form — that's why he holds the lane and solo-kill edge. But none of his tools out-range Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast (600 range vs. his 450/525), so Jayce actually wins the matchup overall (51.9% over 3,196 games) by refusing to fight inside his threat range and poking him down instead.

theirWindow.when: He lands a Q stack on you
theirWindow.what: A second Ntofo Strikes (Q) stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in, opening his Path Maker (W) stun/knockback into a shielded Footwork (E) all-in. Break line of sight or walk back past 450 range right after the first hit instead of trading through it.

yourWindow.what: With his dash/shield down for 8-10s, step up and land a Cannon-stance Shock Blast (Q) or Hyper Charge (W) autos from outside his engage range without fear of a punish dash.

start.why: The highest-performing start (51.5% over 3,446 games, 96% pick) — the extra damage lets your Cannon-stance pokes actually hurt before items, since you can't win sustained melee trades anyway.

boots.why: Best measured win rate of the two options (55.1% over 906 games) — the flat move speed is what lets you hold the 525+ range your whole poke plan depends on against his dash-based engage.

core.why: Fuels the mana you burn spamming Q/W/E to poke instead of trade, and scales directly into Muramana.
Physical damage plus armor shred cuts through his naturally high armor, stacking off the same poke autos and abilities you're already throwing.
Empowers your next auto off mana spent — this is the item that turns your poke from annoying into a real DPS check, typically online around level 11-13.
Directly cuts his Footwork (E) shield and the extra defenses he gains going All Out (R), so your poke damage actually lands instead of getting absorbed.

situational.when: the game goes long and you need the cooldown reduction to keep poking through his repeated all-in windows
you want extra mobility and burst to poke-and-kite rather than ever commit to a full combo
you're ahead and want to threaten a real burst window once his Footwork (E) is on cooldown
you need a cheap active slow to peel his engage off before Cleaver/Muramana are finished

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustains you through the forced melee trades he wins early via Footwork (E) and Path Maker (W), buying time until your poke items come online. Master-tier Jayce players instead run Stormraider's Surge (Sorcery) across 25,036 games — better suited if you're confident enough to never get caught in his engage range at all and want the extra kiting speed instead of sustain.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is both the highest win rate (52.1%) and by far the most-picked setup (77.5%) — Teleport lets you reset top after a poke-and-leave trade instead of ever needing to stand and all-in. Flash+Ignite (51%, 21.6% pick) is a fine alternative if you're ahead and want to force a kill off a landed poke combo.

playing.title: Poke from max range
playing.detail: Fire Cannon-stance Shock Blast (Q, 600 range) from outside his Ntofo Strikes (450 range) and Footwork (525 range) — he physically cannot punish you from there.

playing.title: Punish shield cooldown
playing.detail: Track his Footwork (E, 8-10s cooldown) — once it's used offensively or defensively, you have a clean window to step up and poke before he can dash in or out again.

playing.title: Never feed his 2-stack pull
playing.detail: Don't stand still after he lands one Ntofo Strikes (Q) stack — the second stack fires a pulling shockwave that sets up his whole combo. Walk out past 450 range immediately.

playing.title: Use Acceleration Gate to poke
playing.detail: Drop E (Acceleration Gate) in Cannon stance and fire Shock Blast through it for increased missile speed, range, and damage before his Q/E are back up.

playing.title: Respect Path Maker windup
playing.detail: His W (Path Maker) telegraphs with a charge-up where he takes reduced damage before dashing to knock back and stun. Walk out of its 600 range during the charge rather than trading through it.

playing.title: Swap to Hammer only to finish
playing.detail: Save Hammer-stance Q leap and E knockback for securing a poked-low kill or peeling him off you — don't initiate melee trades into his shield and all-in kit.

playing.title: Play around his All Out timer
playing.detail: After level 6, track his R (All Out, 120/100/80s cooldown). Once it's down, his knockback-through-wall setup is gone — poke freely in that window.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, and the 51.9% Jayce-vs-K'Sante win rate (3,196 games) are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1); the tactical reading — why ranged poke beats his shield-engage despite his lane and solo-kill edge — is my own analysis.
